evidence: Receiving online DO2 drops abruptly from 11.8 mg/L (t≈47.6 h) to 6.2 mg/L (t=47.8 h) and declines monotonically to 4.89 mg/L by t=51.8 h
Extrapolated decline rate ~0.3-0.35 mg/L/h reaches the 2 mg/L hard limit near t≈56-57 h, within the simulated horizon
Delayed product assays show rising product (0 -> 2.7 g/L), so product is being made and mass retention matters
keep is predicted to violate the DO constraint; combined applies both DO-restoring levers while retaining 80% feed
strong_feed_reduction would be more conservative but sacrifices more product mass than evidence indicates is necessary
args.rationale: Receiving DO collapsed from ~11.8 to ~4.9 mg/L over the final 4 hours of observation and is trending toward the 2 mg/L hard limit (~0.3 mg/L/h decline; projected breach near t≈57 h). KEEP is not justifiable. A single-lever fix (increase_air alone) is uncertain against an unquantified oxygen-demand spike; combined applies both a 15% aeration increase and a 20% feed reduction, providing margin on both supply and demand sides of the DO balance while retaining 80% of feed/product trajectory — the best constraint-safety per unit of product mass lost among the available bounded actions.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving-process kinetics (OUR, kLa, feed-spike cause) are unavailable; the decline may be a transient like source-batch dips, or may accelerate. The 15% aeration and 20% feed levers have unverified effect sizes in the receiving vessel. Model mismatch could make even combined marginal; if DO fails to recover by ~54-55 h, a stronger feed reduction or stop would be the next review point. No physical safety is established.
